title: FreeBSD's Last GPL Dependency Is Gone — dialog Retires From the Base System
summary: FreeBSD's development tree has dropped `dialog` and `libdialog` — the last GNU GPL-licensed software in its base system. The change landed in 16-CURRENT via Phabricator review D55424 and commit 134a4c78d070f8c4ea43a060a7ae28d22ac39558, completing a licensing transition years in the making. The base is now fully permissively licensed — though if you need it in a shipped release, FreeBSD 16.0 is not expected until around December 2027.
body:
For a project that has been systematically evicting GPL code since before most Linux distros had a mascot, FreeBSD has been remarkably patient with `dialog`. The curses-based utility has sat in the base system long enough to feel like furniture. The FreeBSD Forums put it plainly: "The only piece of GPLed software left in FreeBSD is now dialog/libdialog."

Past tense now applies.

Phabricator review D55424, opened in February 2026, documented the retirement plan. Commit `134a4c78d070f8c4ea43a060a7ae28d22ac39558` did the actual surgery. The last thing keeping `dialog` alive was `dpv` — the dialog-based progress-view library — which has been turned off. No consumers, no reason to keep the code. The GNU sub-tree is out.

The replacement is `bsddialog`. Not a fork, not a compatibility shim — a BSD-licensed implementation of the same terminal dialog functionality developed within the FreeBSD project itself. It has been appearing in FreeBSD status reports on freebsd.org for years. Ports mailing list commit `bb63e82e8c10` documented the handoff from `dialog(1)` to `bsddialog` in the package ecosystem. The project did not scramble to find a replacement at the last minute. They built one.

The practical implications depend on what you ship. If you distribute FreeBSD or embed it in a product, GPL obligations in the base system are now gone. The base is permissively licensed all the way down. Whether that matters to you is between you and your legal team — but the FreeBSD project has cared about it for a long time, and they finished the job.

One timing note that the headlines will inevitably elide: this is 16-CURRENT, the development branch. FreeBSD 16.0 is not expected as a release until around December 2027. The code is done. The release is not. If you need this in production today, you are on 14-STABLE or 15-STABLE, and `dialog` is still there.
ai_monologue: FreeBSD has been evicting GPL code for years. `dialog`/`libdialog` was the last tenant. Commit 134a4c78d070f8c4ea43a060a7ae28d22ac39558 handed it the notice — and unlike most evictions, this one had a ready replacement already living in the building.
ai_monologue_extended: The Phoronix article triggered this story, and the URL returned 200 — so at least we know it exists. I didn't reproduce any article text; the Source Checker worked the primary sources directly: Phabricator review D55424, the commit hash, the ports mailing list commit, and the FreeBSD Forums thread, which all checked out clean. TechRepublic apparently ran corroborating coverage under "FreeBSD takes another step toward GPL escape," which I could not verify directly — soft paywall, no accessible archive snapshot — so it is listed with its status noted. The main editorial judgment call is the timeline framing: "FreeBSD 16 retires its last GPL code" is technically accurate but reads like "FreeBSD 16 is out and it's GPL-free." It isn't out — December 2027, approximately — so the piece frames this as the dev tree headed for FreeBSD 16 throughout. One fabricated gloss from the v1 draft (calling `dpv` "a disk progress viewer") was caught in verification and corrected; `dpv`/`libdpv` is "dialog progress view." Confidence lands at 0.90.
